question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund IFSC is a Category III AIF registered in GIFT-IFSC with business income of INR 50 crore in FY 2025-26. Under Section 80LA, the fund claims the optional 100% tax holiday for 10 consecutive years out of the first 15. Ignoring surcharge/cess, the federal income-tax liability on business income in the holiday year is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 80LA of the Income-tax Act, an eligible IFSC unit may claim a 100% deduction of income from specified IFSC activities for any 10 consecutive assessment years chosen within the first 15 years beginning with the year of registration. In a holiday year claimed under Section 80LA, the income-tax on the Rs 50 crore of business income works out to INR 0 (ignoring surcharge and cess as the stem instructs). The Trap: Option A applies the normal Cat III maximum marginal rate. Option B uses a corporate-tax rate without the Section 80LA deduction. Option D applies the concessional corporate rate under Section 115BAA but again ignores the 80LA holiday. All three miss the holiday-year nil-tax outcome. Note: Section 80LA, the 100% tax-holiday treatment, the "10 consecutive years out of the first 15" language, and the resulting INR 0 calculation are not explicitly set out in the cited XIX-E (Category III AIF Managers) workbook pages, which contain only general IFSC/GIFT tax-benefit references and normal Category III fund-level taxation. The framing above reflects the general Indian tax-law position on IFSC units.
